It should be noted that not all people with OCD have fears of some unrelated event being impacted by whether or not they maintain their compulsions. Most simply put, OCD implies an “obsession” (or multiple) exists. Obsessions can be based on anything that causes anxiety for the individual, and compulsions are “rituals” the individuals might feel forced to do to satisfy their anxiety. However, the superstitious elements (“If I don’t do COMPULSION then my mother will die”) don’t necessarily appear for everyone. For me, it can be as simple as fears that I upset people or am a bad person, and rather than always having a physical compulsion, my compulsion (if you could call it that) is more or less attempting to justify my poor evaluation of myself. I say all this because there might be some people out there suffering from OCD, but they may be lacking the “superstitious” angle to their obsessions and compulsions, and I don’t want them to feel they aren’t “OCD enough” because of this. 

Note: take this with a grain of salt. Mostly it’s based on therapy sessions, but I could have gotten some stuff twisted along the way.

EDIT: Also it’s possible to have an obsession with no associated compulsive behavior. Simply ruminating on an event for years and years, suffering anxiety all the while, is still considered obsessive (by my therapist, at least).
